edits.find: The infection history is deliberately non-discriminating: eight antibiotic courses for sinusitis and pneumonia is compatible with every option on the list except "normal." The fork is settled by one line of the physical exam — the PMI is in the right chest, i.e. dextrocardia, i.e. situs inversus. Antibody deficiencies do not move the heart; retained secretions do not move the heart; only a disorder of ciliary motility does, because the same dynein-arm defect that leaves airway cilia dysmotile also leaves embryonic nodal cilia unable to establish left–right asymmetry, so laterality is randomized. That converts "recurrent sinopulmonary infection" into Kartagener syndrome — the situs inversus / recurrent sinusitis / bronchiectasis subgroup of primary ciliary dyskinesia. The secondary confirmation is the tonsils: lymphoid tissue is present, which is inconsistent with X-linked agammaglobulinemia.

edits.find: The stem's structure is a two-step gate, and the second step is the one being scored. First, a week of appropriate broad-spectrum antibiotics with no improvement — the explicit trigger for suspecting allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis in cystic fibrosis, because the presentation is otherwise indistinguishable from a cystic fibrosis bronchopneumonia. Second, the two laboratory values that assign a category: eosinophilia and an IgE of 3,225, which is a Th2 allergic response rather than a bacterial one. The mechanism follows from the host — Aspergillus spores are inhaled by everyone and cleared by the mucociliary escalator, but a structurally damaged airway traps them, colonisation becomes chronic, and chronic exposure becomes hypersensitisation. The disease is the immune response, which is why the treatment is a steroid and the antifungal is adjunctive.

edits.find: The sickle cell disease is real, relevant, and not the discriminator. What decides this is a two-word symptom pattern — nocturnal and intermittent — and everything else in the examination exists to remove the alternatives that would have been exertional. Normal vital signs and a normal chest film remove pulmonary embolism, which arrives acute and persistent with tachycardia and hypoxia. No peripheral edema with the apex beat in the fifth intercostal space at the midclavicular line removes pulmonary hypertension and heart failure, both of which announce themselves with right-sided signs or a displaced point of maximal impulse. A normal film with no reticular markings removes fibrosis, which is progressive and exertional. No hilar adenopathy removes sarcoidosis, and the family history of sarcoid is there precisely to make you forget that sarcoid is not associated with sickle cell disease at all. What remains is obstructive airway disease, and asthma is a common comorbidity in children and adolescents with sickle cell disease — so the first test is spirometry, looking for obstruction that reverses with a bronchodilator.
